2. Facts for disposal of the Rule, in short, are that the petitioner Nos. 1-5 Late Haji Mohammad Abul Hafez and predecessor of the petitioner Nos. 6- 12 as plaintiffs instituted other Class Suit No. 112 of 1980 in the 1st Court of Munsif, (now Assistant Judge), Sadar, Chittagong, for a direction upon the defendant Opposite Party No.1 to renewal the Lease Agreement dated 4-9-1949, registered on 12-9-1949 for a further period of 30 years commencing from 1st Aswin, 1386 BS contending inter-alia that the suit land described in the schedule belonged to Late Ashraf Ali Chowdhury in Khas-Dakhali right. The suit land was accredited low lands and was lying in unutilized and vacant condition. Late Haji Ahmed Meah Sowdagar Predecessor of the plaintiffs took lease of the suit land for a period of 30 years at a yearly rent of Taka 1,700 form 1st Aswin, 1356 BS. At the time of execution of the Lease Agreement the predecessor of the petitioners Late Haji Ahmed Meah Sowdagar paid Taka 4,000 as advance rent out of four years rent and balance Taka 2,800 was agreed to be paid along with the annual rent which was paid by Late Haji Ahmed Meah Sowdagar. That Late Haji Ahmed Meah Sowdagar spent huge amount of money in developing the land and in constructing pucca and semipucca house and created Municipal holding in his name. It was one of the conditions that the lease will be renewed for a further period of 30 years after the expiry of lease period at the same rent and on the same terms and conditions. Subsequently, Haji Ashraf Ali Chowdhury created a Wakfnama Deed some time in 1957 and he appointed himself as the first Mutawalli and after his death his son Mohammad Ali Chowdhury Defendant-Opposite Party No. 1 has been appointed as Mutawalli of the wakf Estate. Late Haji Ahmed Meah Sowdagar died leaving seven sons. Haji Hafez Ahmad (died on 20-12-1986, the Daughters of Ahmed Meah Sowdagar relinquished their shares in favour of their brothers. Late Haji Ashraf Ali Chowdhury himself and after his death his successors-in-interest realized rent amicably. Late Ashraf Ali Chowdhury filed Money Suit No. 21 of 1958 in the court of first Subordinate Judge and the suit was decreed. The defendant opposite party No.1 accepted rent up to Bhadra, 1386 as but he refused to accept rent for subsequent period on tender, so the plaintiffs remitted the rent for the period from Aswin, l386 BS to Falgoon, 1386 BS by Money Order and on refusal by the opposite party No.1 the plaintiffs have been depositing rent with the Rent controller in HRC Case No. 23 of 1380 regularly. As per terms and condition of the Lease Agreement the plaintiffs served notice through lawyer on 10-1- 1979 upon the defendant opposite party No. 1 demanding renewal of the Lease Agreement for another period of 30 years commencing from 1st Aswin, 1386 BS the notice has been duly served but the defendant-opposite party No. 1 has not complied with the notice. Hence the suit. 

 3. The suit was contested by the defendant No.1 and 2 by filing written statement denying the material averment made in the plaint. The case of defendant No. 1 is that the disputed property belonged to Late Haji Ashraf Ali Chowdhury. He filed it up at his own cost and raised some construction and let it out to the merchants for carrying goods. Late Ahmed Meah Sowdagar requested Haji Ashraf Ali Chowdhury to allow him to use the schedule land for the purpose of carrying his goods at a monthly rent of Taka 150. Ashraf Ali Chowdhury being busy the Bharanama was drafted by Haji Ahmed Meah Sowdagar from elsewhere. Haji Ashraf Ali Chowdhury in good faith and bonafide belief executed and admitted registration of the same without going through it. The alleged renewal clause is not the averment of Haji Ashraf Ali Chowdhury; as such neither he nor the present Wakif is bound by the same. The Bharanama Agreement being personal agreement between Haji Ashraf Ali Chowdhury and Ahmed Meah Sowdagar, the plaintiff could not inherit any tenancy right in it. The schedule land has been dedicated as Wakf-fi-Sabilillah and it has been duly enrolled in the Wakf Administrator, the alleged renewal clause is not enforceable without prior consent of the Administrator of Wakf. The plaintiffs and their predecessors were habitual defaults. They put the defendant and his predecessor to unnecessary litigation and denied the title of the defendant as such they are not entitled to enquiry. The period of Ekrarnama has expired and as such the same has been extinguished. 

 4. The case of defendant No. 2 is that the schedule land was duly enrolled as wakf property bearing EC No. 13238. The alleged renewal clause is not subject to the consent of this defendant and the same is unauthorized and this defendant is not bound by the same. The schedule land is situated in busy commercial area. The khas possession is essential for making improvement and the proposal for the improvement of the schedule property as per scheme plan and estimate to be submitted by Mutawalli, is required to be implemented soon for better management of the property and enhancement of income of the Wakf Estate. 

 10. Mr Md Harunur Rashid, the learned advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite party No.3 submitted that the appellate court rightly found that the plaintiff has no locus-standi to file the suit since they are not the party to the agreement dated 10-10-1979. The learned advocate further submitted that though the court opined that the tenancy is not heritable but in subsequent decision of our Apex Court reported in 47 DLR (AD) 45 it has been settled that the tenancy is heritable. The learned advocate further submitted that this is not a monthly tenancy as per lease agreement which was for 30 years but as per Section 75 A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act the provision of subletting is prohibited and which came into force on 22-9-1985 by Act 4 of 1956 and will go back to the owner. In support he referred the decision of the case of Abdur Rashed Khan vs Abdus Sam ad Mondal reported in 33 DLR 260. And thus the plaintiff has no locus standi to file the instant suit. Thus the Rule should liable to be discharged. 

 12. The suit is for renewal of the lease agreement. The predecessor of the plaintiffs obtained lease dated 10-10-1979 (Exhibit-1) and in the said agreement theses was a clause for renewal of the agreement. The courts below on consideration of the provision of law opined that the tenancy is not heritable relying upon the decision of 32 DLR (AD) 170 and 38 DLR 806. But in subsequent decision the case of Sova Rani Guha vs Abdul Awal Mia reported in 47 DLR (AD) 45 our Apex Court reviewed the earlier decision and opined that the tenancy is heritable.
